items.title: Gap Mangione interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rochester, New York, January 11, 2012
items.q: we ended up doing the Randall’s Island Jazz Festival opening for a program that included Miles and Coltrane, and Duke Ellington.

ctx.x: Was there a point where you made a conscious decision that I think I can make a living in music, or did it just sort of fall into place?

As a matter of fact I think Chuck and I both, although he did teach for a while, both in terms of semi-private or private lessons, and then of course he started the jazz program essentially at the Eastman School of Music. I think both of us had the idea that we would play until it didn’t work out so well, and then we would get a regular job. So far so good. There was never a, okay we’re going to go for this or we’re going to do that. The kinds of things that happen when you have a recording session and when you…
enough — we were too young to know enough to be scared. We shouldn’t have been there. But of course we were with Sal Nistico, Roy McCurdy, the band was not shy.
